Subject: SIG BCDR: need precise RTO/RPO commitments + evidence

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the SIG questionnaire so far. We need a more granular breakdown on BCDR commitments for our security review — specifically:

- Per-region RTO and RPO for the hosted inference endpoints (normal and high-availability modes)
- Backup cadence and retention for customer data, KV caches, and model artifacts
- Sequence and expected duration for cross-region failover (including DNS/traffic cutover)
- Evidence of most recent DR rehearsal and runbook ownership (dates, owners, artifacts)

Can you also point us to the artifacts (runbooks, test logs, architecture diagram) we can attach to our SIG report? We’re aiming to close this by EOD Tuesday.

Appreciate a short, actionable summary + attachments.

— Aisha

Hi Aisha —

Thanks — flagged to the BCDR team and attaching a short summary plus the playbook and last test logs. High level answers below; details and artifacts attached (see RW_BCDR_Summary_20261130.pdf and runbook_failover_playbook_v3.1.pdf).

• RTO / RPO (hosted inference):
  - Normal HA mode (multi-AZ within a region): RTO target 2 minutes for control-plane failover; RPO < 30s for in-flight requests via continuous KV replication.
  - Cross-region failover (planned regional DR into a paired region): RTO target 15 minutes for full service cutover, RPO < 1 minute for persisted state.
  - Dedicated (reserved) clusters: RTO target 5 minutes for autoscaling/replacement within same region; cross-region commit as above.

• Backups / retention:
  - Customer data (metadata, customer configs): incremental backups every 15 minutes, 30-day rolling retention; encrypted at rest with KMS.
  - KV caches (session/state): continuous replication with periodic snapshots; snapshots retained 7 days by default, configurable for enterprise.
  - Model artifacts: immutable snapshots of model binaries stored in object storage; weekly snapshots retained 90 days, monthly archived as requested.

• Cross-region failover sequence (summary):
  1) Health check escalation & automated policy triggers (0-60s)
  2) Control-plane failover into standby region & KV cache replay (1-5m)
  3) Traffic cutover via weighted DNS + CDN updates (5-10m)
  4) Final verification and routing stabilization (10-15m)

• Rehearsals & evidence:
  - Last full DR rehearsal: 2026-10-12 (quarterly schedule). See attached dr_test_logs_20261012.zip for play-by-play and postmortem.
  - Runbook owner: Karthik Iyer (Infra Reliability) — contact in cc.

If you want, Karthik and I can do a 30-minute walkthrough and share the architecture diagram and Datadog dashboards (link below).

Notes: these are our SLA targets for Redwood-hosted services; specifics for on-prem or private deployments can be configured per contract.

Best,
Lauren

Thanks Lauren — that helps. Two quick clarifications before we finalize:

1) For the cross-region RTO of 15 minutes, can you clarify what portion assumes data replication is already healthy vs. a cold-start of stateful services? In other words: what’s the expected additional recovery time if the KV replication is lagging?

2) Can you confirm whether backups are immutable/append-only for the 90-day model archive (we need assurance against tampering for compliance)?

Also — please include the architecture diagram and the last DR postmortem (we need the postmortem in our SIG submission). If you can attach or link those two items and confirm the answers above, we can close this thread.

— Aisha

Hi Aisha — following up with the technical clarifications and links to the requested artifacts.

1) Cross-region RTO breakdown if KV replication is lagging:
   - If replication is healthy (typical case): cutover timeline as Lauren described (target ~15 minutes).
   - If replication is lagging beyond 60s: automated retransmit and partial replay adds 3–8 minutes depending on backlog size; worst-case (very large backlog) we target 30 minutes to full consistency while serving in degraded read-only for non-idempotent ops. We include versioned snapshots to allow point-in-time restore when necessary.

2) Model archive immutability:
   - Model snapshots are written to immutable object-store buckets with versioning and write-once lifecycle policies by default for hosted customers. Retention and immutability windows are configurable through enterprise contracts; we can provide an audit trail and hash-signed manifests for each snapshot.

Artifacts & links (attached / shared):
   - RW_BCDR_Summary_20261130.pdf (summary with RTO/RPO table and timeline)
   - runbook_failover_playbook_v3.1.pdf (operational playbook, owners, escalation matrix)
   - dr_test_logs_20261012.zip (full logs, screenshots, postmortem)
   - Architecture diagram: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBCdExample/BCDR-Evidence (diagram is in folder)
   - Live dashboards: https://app.datadog.com/dashboard/bcdr-redwood

Additional context: our quarterly drills include a table-top, staged failover, and smoke-validation on real traffic in a canary slice. Last full exercise demonstrated service restoration to 95% traffic within 12 minutes (control-plane + KV replay). Postmortem included two action items (improved snapshot frequency and alert tuning) which are closed.

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough next week and I’ll include DR runbook owners. Proposed times: Tue 12/7 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 12/8 14:00–14:30 PT.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
